Use the reference as a grayscale spatial relief guide for the motor locations.

Studio product photograph of one compact camera drone for everyday personal aerial photography, seen from directly above in a strict orthographic top view, centered on a seamless white background with a soft contact shadow. A quadcopter with four arms, one motor at the end of each arm and one two-blade propeller on each motor. The nose points toward the top edge of the picture. A small forward-facing gimbal camera sits under the nose; from above only the top of its housing shows at the front edge, and the lens faces forward, not upward. Design the body silhouette, the arm sections and the way the arm roots blend into the body freely. Materials: fine-textured matte polycarbonate body shell in light warm gray, darker graphite-gray arms and motor mounts, satin anodized aluminium motor bells, semi-gloss black propellers, glossy black camera glass, thin precise panel seams. Soft overhead softbox lighting with gentle highlights on edges and chamfers. The left-right motor spacing is 0.70 times the front-back motor spacing.

Avoid: flat shading, vector illustration, schematic, line drawing, clay render, blurry, text, labels, logo, cropped propeller, disconnected arm, extra rotor, propeller guard, perspective view, lens facing the viewer
